# taxifydb

*building taxonomic backbones and trait tables from their sources*

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/gcol33/taxifydb/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/gcol33/taxifydb)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
<!-- badges: end -->

taxifydb builds the files that [taxify](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/) matches species names against: taxonomic backbones such as the Catalogue of Life or World Flora Online, trait and status datasets, and region polygons.

Each builder downloads a source from its provider, converts it to the column layout that every taxify backbone shares, and writes a `.vtr` file, the on-disk table format of [vectra](https://gillescolling.com/vectra/). taxify downloads these files ready-built, so name matching never needs taxifydb. You install taxifydb when you want to build a file yourself, from a newer snapshot or for a source taxify does not host, add a backbone or dataset, or republish the hosted files. taxifydb supports:

- **Taxonomic backbones.** `r n_backbones` backbones, from global checklists to the authorities of single groups, are built through `build_backend()` and share one layout: the name, its identifier, its taxonomic status, the family and genus, and the link to the accepted name.
- **Trait and status datasets.** `r n_enrichments` trait, ecology, conservation and invasion datasets, called enrichments in the function names, are parsed to one row per species or genus and resolved to accepted names, so they join the output of any backbone.
- **Region polygons.** Botanical regions and marine ecoregions are built and versioned like a backbone; taxify reads them to restrict matching to a region.
- **Publishing releases.** `publish_release()` and `publish_enrichment_release()` upload built files as GitHub release assets and record each one in the manifest that taxify reads.

The manifest records each published file with its version and the hash of its bytes. taxify reads it to find its downloads and to tell a stale copy from a current one, and a weekly workflow in the repository reports a release, an asset or a manifest entry that has fallen out of step.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/taxifydb")
```

## Usage

1. Build a backbone with `build_backend()`.
2. Build a dataset with `build_enrichment()`.
3. Rebuild the tables that resolve dataset names across backbones with `build_all_name_lookups()`.

```r
library(taxifydb)

itis_vtr <- build_backend("itis")
clopla_vtr <- build_enrichment("clopla")
build_all_name_lookups()
```

Each build downloads the full source from its provider and returns the path of the `.vtr` file it wrote, under `output/` in the working directory. taxify builds through taxifydb when a ready-built download is not available. `list_backends()`, `list_geometry()` and `list_enrichments()` list what can be built.

## Backbones

| Backbone | Scope |
|---|---|
| WFO | World Flora Online (plants) |
| COL | Catalogue of Life (all kingdoms) |
| COL XR | Catalogue of Life Extended Release (all kingdoms) |
| GBIF | Backbone Taxonomy of the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (all kingdoms) |
| ITIS | Integrated Taxonomic Information System |
| NCBI | Taxonomy of the US National Center for Biotechnology Information |
| OTT | Open Tree of Life synthesis |
| WoRMS | World Register of Marine Species |
| Euro+Med | Euro+Med PlantBase (European and Mediterranean plants) |
| Index Fungorum | Fungi |
| AlgaeBase | Algae |
| FishBase | Fishes |
| SeaLifeBase | Aquatic species other than fishes |
| Reptile Database | Reptiles |
| WCVP | World Checklist of Vascular Plants (Kew) |
| LCVP | Leipzig Catalogue of Vascular Plants |
| MDD | Mammal Diversity Database |
| AviList | Birds |
| LPSN | List of Prokaryotic names with Standing in Nomenclature (Bacteria and Archaea) |

The region polygons are the botanical regions of the World Geographical Scheme for Recording Plant Distributions (WGSRPD, level 3) and the Marine Ecoregions of the World (MEOW). They hold polygon vertices instead of names, so `list_geometry()` lists them apart from the backbones. [The backbones and datasets](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/databases.html) in the taxify documentation describes each backbone and dataset with its version, licence and reference.

## Hosting the built files

Built files are published as GitHub release assets: one tag per backbone release, such as `gbif-2026.08`, and one tag per enrichment release, such as `enrichment-2026.10`, that holds every dataset. `manifest/manifest.json` records each asset's version, address and content hash, and taxify reads it to find its downloads. `update_manifest()` and `update_enrichment_manifest()` keep the build-side and runtime manifests in step.

## Sources that need extra software

Some builders need an optional package: [RSQLite](https://cran.r-project.org/package=RSQLite) for ITIS, [openxlsx2](https://cran.r-project.org/package=openxlsx2) for Excel sources, [rfishbase](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rfishbase) for FishBase and SeaLifeBase, [GIFT](https://cran.r-project.org/package=GIFT) for the GIFT database. A builder that needs one stops with a message naming the package to install.

A few sources sit behind Cloudflare or a publisher's bot check and are fetched with a bundled Python helper. The interpreter is taken from the environment variable `TAXIFYDB_PYTHON` when it is set, and otherwise found among the pyenv and system installations.

## Adding a backbone or dataset

A backbone needs a builder registered in `build_backend()`, a dataset a parser and a registry entry. `CLAUDE.md` in the repository lists every step and the column layout each file must follow.

## Documentation

Start with the help page of `build_backend()`: what a build downloads, where it writes the file and what it returns.

- [The backbones and datasets](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/databases.html): each backbone and dataset with its version, licence and reference, in the taxify documentation.
- [Choosing and combining backbones](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/backbones.html): how taxify downloads, chains and pins the files built here.
- `help(package = "taxifydb")`: every exported builder, checker and publisher.

## Getting help

Questions and bug reports go to the [GitHub issues](https://github.com/gcol33/taxifydb/issues). A bug report is easiest to act on with a small reproducible example, for instance made with [reprex](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/).

The code of taxifydb is licensed under MIT. Each source dataset keeps its own licence. Only openly licensed data is redistributed through the releases of this repository; sources that permit citation only or carry no licence are built locally and never redistributed. When you use a dataset's data, cite the original dataset.

## Citation

```{r citation, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cit <- citation("taxifydb")
fence <- function(lang, x) cat("```", lang, "\n", paste(x, collapse = "\n\n"), "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
cat(attr(cit, "mheader"), "\n\n", sep = "")
fence("text", format(cit, style = "text"))
cat("BibTeX:\n\n")
fence("bibtex", format(cit, style = "bibtex"))
```
